options: Float on top of the fuel
Mix in and turn the fuel clear
Settle to the bottom of the tank
Increase the energy content of the fuel
questions.explanation: Water is denser than diesel. Drain from the lowest point.

options: A bilge holding tank for oily water
A tank for drinking water for the crew
A tank for sewage between pump-outs
A small tank near the engine that feeds it
questions.explanation: It is topped up from the main tanks.

questions.stem: Diesel fuel has a specific gravity of about:
options: 0.65, much lighter than water
0.85, lighter than water
1.5, heavier than water
1.05, a little heavier than water
questions.explanation: Diesel floats on water, which is why water collects under fuel.

options: Microbial growth that forms sludge and clogs filters
Insects that get into the fuel through the tank vents
Corrosion flakes from the tank walls and baffles
An additive that keeps the fuel clean in storage
questions.explanation: They grow at the fuel and water boundary. Keep tanks free of water.

questions.stem: Which is the best way to handle fuel-soaked rags?
options: Throw them over the side when well offshore
Pile them behind the engine until port
Leave them spread on the engine to dry out
Keep them in a closed metal bin for proper disposal
questions.explanation: Fuel-soaked rags are a fire hazard and a pollutant.

questions.stem: The best way to check fuel is not contaminated before a voyage is to:
options: Check the colour through the tank sight glass
Look at the fuel gauge only before you sail
Smell the tank vent for any sour odour
Drain and inspect a sample from the lowest point
questions.explanation: Water and sediment collect at the bottom.

questions.stem: A tank holds 800 litres of fuel and the engine burns 20 litres an hour. At that rate the endurance is:
options: 4 hours
16 hours
160 hours
40 hours

questions.stem: A sounding pipe that ends in a machinery space is normally fitted with:
options: A fuel heater
A self-closing cock or cap
A pressure relief valve
A loose screw cap on a chain
questions.explanation: An open sounding pipe in a machinery space is a fuel and fire hazard.

questions.stem: Before starting an inboard gasoline engine you should:
options: Open the engine room hatches and start at once
Switch off the bilge pump to stop any sparks
Fill the fuel tank right to the top so no vapour can form
Run the bilge blower and check the bilge for vapour
questions.explanation: Gasoline vapour sinks into the bilge and can explode. Ventilate before starting.

questions.stem: When transferring fuel between tanks you should:
options: Rely only on the gauge and leave the tank to fill
Fill the receiving tank to the brim for the voyage
Start the pump and leave it running while you do other jobs
Check space, set valves, keep vents clear, watch the level
questions.explanation: Plan, check the line-up, and stay with the transfer until it is stopped.
